title: Finite reduction of the tensor form before reassociation
statement: In the finite setting P let 1 <= m <= P.level and Q be the smaller setting. Let f:X -> Y be smooth separated of relative dimension d between separated finite-type base schemes. For intrinsic finite-Tor constructible K on Y, let t_P(K)=smoothPurityTensorMap f d K, the realized (1 tensor Pi inverse) followed by theta, before applying tau [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. With the independent tensor-source comparison c_tensor [def-pur-finite-reduction-tensor-source] and the counit-normalized exceptional comparison c_exc [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons], red_X(t_P(K)) followed by c_exc(K) equals c_tensor(K) followed by t_Q(red_Y K). No reassociation tau or full smoothPurityMap occurs in this assertion.

proof.text: Extract etale presentations of K and its reduction from compositionInput_bounded and plusEtaleOrigin. The defining characterization of smoothPurityTensorMap and functoriality write both purity maps as the realized inverse-orientation factor followed by the realized theta factor.

Take the last equality of diagonalOrientationReduction. Identify its proTwistMap with finiteTensorPositiveReduction using the positive-line comparison. Invert the resulting orientation square. The naturality field of finiteTensorCore moves inverse orientation through its inverse tensorator. Tensor interchange with the input/pullback comparison gives the fixed-coordinate inverse-orientation square. Naturality of scalarPresentation and functoriality of realization give the intrinsic inverse-orientation square.

Expand reduction of the two-factor composite by Functor.map_comp. Substitute the theta factor square. Reassociate, substitute the inverse-orientation square, and reassociate once more. The intermediate omega comparison cancels by pasting, proving the stated square.
